answer: To keep a sybil farm expensive, admission starts at a kernel of slashable collateral locked for four epochs. The applicant must then wander a seed-tied circuit of live work issued by five established peers, each of whom posts a smaller endorse bond. Only after those peers attest distinct, non-overlapping receipts does the seat gain grading weight. If a later audit shows cloned signing paths, both the timber deposit and the endorsers' bonds are slashed, and re-entry restarts the clock at a doubled stake, so aliases cost capital, calendar time, and unique work rather than a free signup.
